  • Confident in competitive sales cycles, able to articulate differentiation and handle objections effectively.
  • Analytical, detail-oriented, and accountable for forecast accuracy and pipeline hygiene.
  • Resilient, driven, and passionate about helping customers realize long-term value through partnership.
  • Excited by innovation and transformation — particularly the opportunity to represent a next-generation AI-powered communications platform.

    At Aircall, you’ll join a fast-moving, customer-obsessed team that thrives at the intersection of success and growth. You’ll have the autonomy to build your book of business, the support of dedicated technical partners, and the opportunity to help customers unlock the full potential of Aircall’s communications and AI solutions.

Date limite de candidature : 15/11/2026

________________________

Environnement professionnel

L’Agence de services et de paiement est un organisme de paiement public dédié à la mise en place de politiques publiques, au service d’une société plus durable et plus solidaire.

Vous rejoindrez la Direction du développement rural et de la pêche (DDRP), en charge de la mise en œuvre de l’ensemble des mesures du développement rural (FEADER hors aides surfaciques, nombreuses aides nationales, ainsi que celles liées à la pêche) et qui assure la maîtrise d'ouvrage des outils de gestion des fonds européens et des aides nationales.

Pour exercer sa mission, la DDRP s'appuie sur un réseau de directions régionales (DR) qui couvre l'ensemble du territoire.

Vous exercerez votre mission dans le service métier des aides au développement rural et à la pêche (SADRP) au sein du secteur des aides nationales et FEADER (SANF).

Ce secteur est notamment en charge du déploiement des dispositifs d’aides nationales dans SAFRAN côté métier, en lien avec la direction des opérations (DO) côté outil.

Objectifs

Vous occuperez un poste de chef de projet avec un rôle de product manager officer (PMO):

  • Coordonner côté métier la maîtrise d'ouvrage du déploiement des dispositifs (aides nationales, aides FEADER pour certaines régions) dans SAFRAN (outil d’instruction) ainsi que dans l’écosystème des outils liés (gestion des enveloppes, contrôle, …)

  • Contribuer dans ce domaine, en appui à la cheffe de secteur, à la définition des objectifs assignés à l’équipe des référents de dispositifs nationaux, à l’organisation des activités, l’accompagnement au changement

  • Co-animer le réseau des référents SAFRAN des directions régionales (DR) de l’ASP

Missions

Pilotage métier du déploiement des dispositif dans l'outil SAFRAN et l'écosystème associé

  • Coordonner et animer le recueil des besoins métiers pour l’outil SAFRAN (instruction des aides) en lien avec l’écosystème des outils liés (gestion des enveloppes, contrôle, …) et le déploiement des dispositifs

  • Co-piloter la feuille de route de déploiement des dispositifs en lien avec la direction des opérations et co-animer les instances de pilotage associées

  • Alerter sur les difficultés (auprès de la DDRP et au donneur d’ordre), proposer des solutions

  • Animer le groupe référents dispositifs du SANF et suivre avec eux l'instrumentation, le recettage et la mise en production de SAFRAN, assurer le suivi dans des outil de gestion de projet

Contribuer à l’animation du réseau des référents SAFRAN en D(i)R-ASP

  • Coanimer le réseau des référents SAFRAN en D(i)R – ASP en lien avec la direction des opérations (DO)

  • Copiloter avec la DO les formations des membres du réseau

  • Assurer la veille sur les évolutions de l’outil et les partager

Contribuer à l’amélioration des pratiques et au suivi des activités (reporting)

  • Dans le domaines des dispositifs nationaux : contribuer à la préparation des réunions de secteur, contribuer à établir et à faire vivre les outils de suivi de l’activité et des projets, s'assurer du respect des échéances

  • Participer à des bilatérales avec les agents en charge des dispositifs nationaux

  • Participer aux réunions des cadres du SADRP et aux points cadres de la direction

Champ relationnel

Vous serez au contact

  • en interne : avec les autres équipes de la direction, d’autres directions du Siège de l’ASP, les directions régionales de l’ASP

  • en externe : avec les  ministères en charge de l’agriculture et de la transition écologique notamment et les services déconcentrés de l’Etat (DRAAF, DDT), le cas échéant.

Savoirs

  • Maîtrise de l’environnement de l’ASP, de son fonctionnement et de ses enjeux.

  • Maîtrise de la gouvernance mise en œuvre pour la gestion des aides nationales et européennes

  • Gestion de projets

Savoir-faire

  • Aisance dans la communication orale et écrite

  • Pilotage de projet, coordination

  • Accompagnement au changement

  • Organisation, méthode, gestion des priorités et des délais

  • Suivi et reporting

Savoir-être

  • Qualités relationnelles, capacité d’écoute et d’animation

  • Capacités d’adaptation et d’initiative

  • Capacité d’entrainement

  • Sens de la communication et pédagogie

  • Capacité d’analyse critique et savoir prendre du recul

  • Réactivité

  • Autonomie

Conditions particulières d’exercice

Télétravail possible dans la limite des conditions définies au sein de l’ASP.

05 55 12 06 30

description: <p>Apaleo is the world’s most open, API-first property management platform powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Its modular, AI-powered infrastructure enables hoteliers to customise their tech stack, automate routine work, and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.</p> <h3>Why this role</h3> <p>You are the technical voice in front of strategic customers, at a moment when hospitality is being rebuilt around AI. We are launching our own AI agent platform, and we need architects who can show operators what comes next.</p> <ul> <li><strong>High trust.</strong> You own the technical answer in front of strategic customers and deals.</li> <li><strong>High visibility.</strong> Your work shows up in deals, key accounts and customer stories, and it reaches Product.</li> <li><strong>High freedom.</strong> You decide how to solve a problem, which tools to use and what to prototype.</li> <li><strong>Fast iteration.</strong> We test ideas within days, try new technology early and share what works.</li> </ul> <h3>Your mission</h3> <p>Win and grow strategic accounts with technical credibility, and turn what you learn in the field into input for the product. You look at a customer's current architecture and show how an Apaleo-centred setup delivers their goals. You also help them put AI agents to work, deciding what should be an agent, what it costs and how to set it up. Sales and Account Management own the relationship and the commercial terms. You own the technical answer.</p> <h3>What you will do</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Technical discovery and solution scoping.</strong> Lead discovery where a standard demo is not enough. Write clear scopes covering what Apaleo delivers natively, what needs a short-term solution and what is out of scope.</li> <li><strong>Proofs of concept.</strong> Build fast, working proofs of concept (quick demos that show technical fit). Agree scope in writing first, and build in a safe test environment, never with live guest data.</li> <li><strong>Agents and automations.</strong> Design and build agents and automations for customer use cases, using n8n or Make today and Apaleo's own AI agent platform as it launches. Write code where agents need deterministic steps.</li> <li><strong>Hands-on delivery and short-term solutions.</strong> Work alongside the customer, building only where it unblocks a named deal, removes an adoption risk or fills a product gap. Agree an exit plan (an end date, a replacement and a named owner) before you start.</li> <li><strong>Post-sale health checks and expansions.</strong> Diagnose gaps against the go-live specification, run proactive checks (for example 90 days after go-live) and scope integrations for expanding customers.</li> <li><strong>Reusable assets.</strong> Turn every engagement into a reference architecture, pattern or template that the next twenty customers can use.</li> <li><strong>Thought leadership.</strong> Join prospect and customer conversations on how AI will change hospitality over the next two to three years.</li> <li><strong>Product feedback.</strong> Test new technology on real customer problems. Share prototypes and field evidence with Product, ending every experiment with a clear decision: adopt, hand over or drop.</li> </ul> <h3>How you work</h3> <ul> <li>You decide the approach, the stack and the order of work.</li> <li>You protect three guardrails: written scope before a proof of concept, an exit plan before a custom build and no commercial promises.</li> <li>You go from idea to prototype in days and show it early.</li> <li>You think in systems and build for reuse, not one-off projects.</li> <li>You share findings openly with Sales, Account Management and Product.</li> </ul> <h3>Who you work with</h3> <p>Sales/BD and Account Management (they call you in at defined deal triggers), Customer Success, Product, Security, Partnerships, RevOps and Senior Leadership.&nbsp;</p> <h3>What you bring</h3> <p><strong>Must have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Multiple years in solution architecture, solution engineering or technical consulting in B2B SaaS, ideally with complex software such as ERP or enterprise platforms</li> <li>Strong API skills: REST, authentication, webhooks and events, and data-flow design</li> <li>Hands-on workflow automation (n8n preferred) and practical experience building with LLM agents</li> <li>A systems thinker with real AI curiosity, who uses AI tools day to day</li> <li>Stakeholder management experience and credibility with executives and IT teams</li> <li>Self-direction, an ownership mindset and the discipline to say no to scope that does not advance a deal</li> <li>Curiosity that ends in working prototypes, not just opinions</li> <li>Clear, structured documentation habits</li> <li>Fluent English and French skills</li> <li>Willingness to travel, including regularly to France and the UK</li> </ul> <p><strong>Strong plus</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hospitality or travel experience, including hotel operations and PMS concepts (reservations, folios, rate plans, night audit)</li> <li>Experience with another cloud PMS, channel manager or payments integrations</li> <li>Enterprise architecture experience on large, multi-site projects</li> <li>Applied AI or ML background, or experience with MCP and agent platforms</li> <li>SQL and BI fundamentals</li> </ul> <h3>How we measure success</h3> <ul> <li>Architecture engagements and blueprints delivered each quarter</li> <li>Customer satisfaction with your contribution</li> <li>Adoption of recommended apps, integrations and agents</li> <li>Share of engagements served by an existing reusable pattern</li> <li>Revenue impact e.g. deal unblocked, AI adoption, or churn averted</li> </ul> <h3>Your first 90 days</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Days 1 to 30:</strong> Learn the platform and ways of working, shadow discovery and proof of concept work, and take over open customer projects.</li> <li><strong>Days 31 to 60:</strong> Lead technical discovery on live deals and run your first health check with Account Management.</li> <li><strong>Days 61 to 90:</strong> Deliver a proof of concept or short-term solution end to end with an exit plan, and share your first experiment with Product.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3><strong>What We Offer</strong></h3> <h3><strong>Culture &amp; Growth</strong></h3> <ul> <li><strong>A Diverse &amp; International Team:</strong>&nbsp;Work alongside passionate professionals from over 20 nationalities, bringing unique cultural perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences to shape the future of hospitality tech.</li> <li><strong>Growth &amp; Development:</strong>&nbsp;As we scale, so do your opportunities. You’ll benefit from 360° feedback reviews, a dedicated learning budget, and plenty of chances to take on more responsibility. Our evolving career framework ensures you have increasing opportunities to learn new skills, advance your career, and make an impact.</li> <li><strong>Autonomy &amp; Ownership:</strong>&nbsp;Great ideas can come from anywhere. About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

Evaluation is how we decide which models, checkpoints and recipes ship. As a Research Engineer on the Eval Platform team, you will build the infrastructure every science team relies on to measure model quality, and make it reliable, reproducible and fast.

You don't need to have designed benchmarks before. You do need to care about what a score means, and about when a difference between two runs is real.

What you will do

  • Build systems that keep eval results reproducible and comparable over time, as models, benchmarks and code evolve.

  • Run evaluations at scale across our GPU clusters, from model serving to scoring.

  • Make eval results easy to access, explore and trust, through APIs and dashboards that researchers use every day.

  • Catch broken or noisy evals before they mislead research decisions.

  • Support evaluation of agentic, multi-turn and tool-using models.

  • Work closely with researchers to turn new evaluation needs into robust, shared tooling.

What we're looking for

  • Master's or PhD in Computer Science, or equivalent experience.

  • 4+ years building production-grade software, ideally large-scale ML codebases or distributed systems.

  • Excellent Python and strong software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD.

  • Experience running workloads on GPU clusters (Slurm, Kubernetes, Ray or similar).

  • Familiarity with LLM inference and evaluation.

  • A product mindset: researchers are your users.

  • Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative.

Nice to have

  • Experience building or maintaining evaluation harnesses or benchmarks.

  • Hands-on experience with inference engines such as vLLM or SGLang.

  • Experience with agentic or RL environments.

  • Statistics for experimentation: variance estimation, significance testing.

  • Open-source contributions to ML tooling.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

title: Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>About Electra</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Air travel is about to become something more: more direct, more accessible, and more connected to the places where people live, work and want to be. Every day in the U.S., people make 35 million trips of 50–500 miles, stuck in traffic or routed through crowded hubs. Chances are, you've been one of them. At Electra, we're changing that with the EL9, a nine-passenger, hybrid-electric aircraft that takes off and lands in just 150 feet. Our Ultra Short technology opens up thousands of new places to fly, beyond conventional runways, congested airports and long drives. We're backed by Lockheed Martin, Honeywell and Safran. Operators worldwide have signed intent-to-purchase agreements for the first 2,200 aircraft we produce, and we're moving toward first test flights in 2027.</span></p> <p><span style="font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Getting a new kind of aircraft airborne takes more than ambition. It takes our kind of bold: people who think big while working in the real world. Who move ideas into action and collaborate without silos. Who put people first and make room at the table for everyone. Who challenge one another without diminishing one another.</span></p> <p><span style="font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Sound like you? Then look beyond what you thought were your own limits, and help us take flight beyond runways.</span></p></div><p><strong>The Role</strong></p> <p>As Electra's Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer, you'll play a key role in developing and industrializing the structural assembly processes for the EL9 aircraft, working from early product development through prototype build, production implementation, and ramp-up.</p> <p>You'll work closely with Product Engineering during aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and can be efficiently, repeatably, and reliably produced. You'll bring a hands-on manufacturing perspective to structural design decisions, evaluating assembly sequence, tolerance management, access, tooling, fastening and joining methods, inspection requirements, producibility, and production risk.</p> <p>As the EL9 transitions from design into physical hardware, you'll help translate released engineering into executable manufacturing processes and support prototype and initial aircraft builds. You'll work closely with airframe manufacturing suppliers, providing on-site Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support as needed to ensure proper information flow, resolve technical and quality issues, support the incorporation of product changes and support supply chain on contract management.</p> <p>This is an opportunity to influence both how the aircraft is designed and how it is ultimately built, while helping establish Electra's structural assembly manufacturing supply chain capability from the ground up.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Product Engineering throughout aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and support efficient, repeatable, and scalable production.</li> <li>Review aircraft structural designs, assemblies, drawings, models, and engineering changes from a manufacturing perspective, providing recommendations related to producibility, assembly sequence, access, tolerance stack-up, fastening and joining methods, tooling, inspection, and production risk.</li> <li>Participate in design trade studies, concept reviews, and design reviews, representing Manufacturing Engineering and identifying manufacturing constraints and opportunities early in the development cycle.</li> <li>Provide Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support at airframe and structural suppliers, working directly with supplier manufacturing teams to clarify design and manufacturing intent, resolve producibility and assembly issues, and maintain program execution.</li> <li>Work closely with the airframe supplier Tooling Engineering to define assembly tooling concepts, requirements, locating strategies, interfaces, and implementation plans.</li> <li>Review supplier manufacturing approaches, build plans, assembly processes, tooling concepts, and production readiness to ensure alignment with Electra's engineering requirements and program objectives.</li> <li>Support prototype fabrication, development aircraft assembly, first builds, and production implementation, providing hands-on Manufacturing Engineering support to resolve issues encountered during structural assembly.</li> <li>Coordinate technical resolution of manufacturing issues and nonconformances with Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders.</li> <li>Capture manufacturing lessons learned and supplier feedback from prototype and initial production builds and drive those learnings back into product design, manufacturing processes, tooling, and planning.</li> <li>Support structural assembly production ramp-up by identifying constraints, resolving manufacturing issues, improving assembly processes, and driving improvements in quality, cost, schedule, and production rate.</li> <li>Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Electra manufacturing engineering standards, methods, processes, and best practices.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Aeronautical, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering field.</li> <li>8+ years of aerospace manufacturing engineering experience, with significant experience in aircraft structural assembly and industrialization.</li> <li>Strong hands-on knowledge of aircraft structural assembly processes, including metallic and/or composite airframe structures, drilling, fastening, joining, shimming, sealing, alignment, and major structural integration.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience applying Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles during aircraft product development.</li> <li>Experience reviewing engineering drawings, 3D models, GD&amp;T, tolerances, and engineering changes from a manufacturing and assembly perspective.</li> <li>Experience developing manufacturing plans, assembly sequences, work instructions, tooling requirements, and manufacturing engineering documentation.</li> <li>Experience supporting prototype, development, or first-production aircraft builds.</li> <li>Experience working directly with aircraft structures suppliers or manufacturing partners and supporting production activities in a factory environment.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work effectively across Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, Tooling, and Production organizations.</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills and ability to make sound engineering recommendations in a fast-moving aircraft development environment.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across internal teams and external suppliers.</li> <li>Ability and willingness to travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as required by program needs.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Points</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with clean-sheet aircraft development and transition from prototype into production.</li> <li>Experience with major structural assemblies such as fuselage, wing, empennage, control surfaces, or other primary airframe structures.</li> <li>Experience with aircraft assembly tooling, jigs, fixtures, determinant assembly, or advanced assembly methodologies.</li> <li>Experience with digital manufacturing tools, PLM/MES environments, manufacturing BOMs, and 3D model-based manufacturing.</li> <li>Experience with supplier industrialization, production readiness assessments, or manufacturing capability reviews.</li> <li>Experience with MRB, root cause corrective action, and production nonconformance resolution.</li> <li>Experience with AS9100 aerospace quality management systems.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus. 2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer. 3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus. Why us? Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate. No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title. We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one. Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP). Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible. Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together. Process Expectations.   • Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result.
  • Coach the customer hands-on. In trials and hackathons, the customer drives and you navigate: you get them to enter their own real legal questions, create the first "wow" moment themselves, and build the habits (saved prompts, reusable workflows) that make them stay.
  • Turn objections into use cases. When a customer says "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves," you respond with a concrete path: a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative. You're straight about limits, because credibility is what closes.
  • Speak at eye level with GCs and legal teams asking sharp discovery questions, translating their friction points into what the product can do, and framing value in their language (ROI, risk, time saved).
  • Always leave with a next step. Trial licenses, a hackathon, a follow-up workshop, a scoped rollout conversation. You instinctively convert interest into momentum, and you remove friction ("we can make that happen") rather than adding process. 2. Legal foundation. Solid legal training and hands-on experience with commercial contracts from in-house, law firm, or legal tech. You understand the "why" behind a clause and can teach that logic to an AI and to a customer. A German 2. Staatsexamen is welcome but not required: we explicitly encourage candidates with qualifications from other jurisdictions or non-traditional paths (e.g. law + IT).

3. Hands-on AI builder. You have spent serious time with LLMs, not as a spectator, but pushing them to their limits. You see prompting and evaluation as a craft and enjoy figuring out where AI systems break and how to fix them.

4. Ownership & communication. You can point to things you built, launched, or drove. You are structured enough to run projects with multiple stakeholders, and precise enough to know that a sharp prompt beats a thousand vague instructions. Excellent German and English; other languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, revenue, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • Leverage, not grind. You build the standards, playbooks, and demos that multiply your expertise across the whole company.

About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a Public Sector Enterprise Account Executive II to join our Sales team.

Our sales team is tenured, technically curious, and genuinely invested in doing right by the customer. We partner closely across the business, and we operate with a lot of trust: you're given real ownership over your territory, and you're expected to bring your own judgment to how you build it.

As an Enterprise Account Executive II, you'll own the full sales cycle for a defined set of Public Sector enterprise accounts, from first conversation through negotiation and close, partnering with sales engineering, customer success, and your manager to navigate complex deals. This role matters because enterprise wins are how Camunda grows its footprint in large accounts, and how we prove the platform works at scale.

This role gives you a book of enterprise accounts to grow and a real say in how you build your territory. You'll work complex deals with multiple stakeholders, and you'll have the support of sales engineering and customer success behind you as you build credibility and close. Camunda’s capabilities are well-aligned to the use cases that will help the DACH Administration digitize and automate for more efficiency and agility - this is an opportunity to shape and build a large and meaningful business!

What You Will Do

  • Build a territory plan that identifies Land opportunities and Expand possibilities, leveraging your extended resources such as Partners, Marketing, Inside Sales, Customer Success.

  • Build account plans that identify whitespace, map stakeholders, and set a realistic path to close.

  • Navigate multi-stakeholder buying committees, including technical, business, and economic buyers.

  • Own and execute the full sales cycle, from prospecting through negotiation and close.

  • Partner with sales engineering and customer success to build technical credibility and ensure a smooth handoff and adoption after close.

  • Represent Camunda's value to business and technical buyers, tailoring the message to what each audience actually cares about.

  • Handle tender processes with precision, observe pipeline health with discipline, manage Forecast with accuracy.

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • Solid experience closing enterprise software deals end-to-end in DACH, with a track record across multiple full sales cycles. You know what it takes to move a deal from first meeting to signature without losing momentum.

  • Efficient balance between driving towards a customer vision and achieving short-term projects towards this horizon.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with own initiative. The playbook will not provide all answers in advance!

  • Comfort navigating multi-stakeholder enterprise environments. You've worked complex deals involving IT, business, and procurement stakeholders, and you know how to keep everyone moving in the same direction.

  • Developing territory and account planning instincts, orchestrating resources efficiently. You can build a plan with some independence, not just work from a list handed to you, and you're learning to prioritize where your time actually pays off.

  • Experience navigating complex public procurement procedures - knowing and following the processes but also influencing them with initiative and creativity.

  • Comfort selling technical products. Experience with process automation, integration platforms, middleware, or similar technical software is a real advantage here, particularly in a Public Sector context, since you'll regularly be in the room with engineering and IT buyers.

  • Negotiation experience under real pressure. You know where to hold firm and where to flex, and you can explain your reasoning either way.

  • A relationship-building style that goes beyond the transaction. You've had customers start to treat you as an advisor, not just a vendor.

If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on</span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto"> </span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto">In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare&nbsp;disease, and&nbsp;develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible. </span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto"> </span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto">Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical &amp; thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;134233117&quot;:true,&quot;134233118&quot;:true,&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559740&quot;:240}">&nbsp;</span></p></div><p>&nbsp;</p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">About BridgeBio Pharma, Inc.&nbsp;</span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing, and delivering transformative medicines for patients living with genetic diseases and genetically defined cancers. Since our founding in 2015, we have built a diverse portfolio of more than 20 drug development programs, ranging from early discovery to late-stage clinical trials, across multiple therapeutic areas including precision oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, and renal disease. We have already achieved regulatory approval for three therapies and continue to advance promising science from academia into meaningful treatments for patients worldwide.&nbsp;</p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Who We Are&nbsp;</span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a global biotechnology company with our Global Headquarters located in San Francisco, USA, and our International HQ located in Zug, Switzerland. Since establishing our European presence in 2021, we’ve been building empowered, high-performing teams across countries — with experienced colleagues who move quickly, take ownership, and are fueling the company’s international growth.&nbsp;</p> <p>At BridgeBio, you’ll find an energetic and collaborative culture where pragmatism meets bold decision-making. We embrace uncertainty with confidence, guided by our commitment to making a meaningful impact for patients. Our people are trusted and empowered, united by urgency, purpose, and the drive to advance science for patients around the world.&nbsp;</p> <p>To learn more about our story and company culture, visit us at <a href="https://bridgebio.com">https://bridgebio.com</a></p> <p><strong><u>What You’ll Do</u></strong></p> <p>You will report to the VP, Head of Market Access, International and work closely with international Market Access, regional brand team, and heads or markets access in BridgeBio clusters as well as with field-based colleagues across multiple geographies, to drive strategic initiatives that support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients globally.</p> <p>Your primary purpose will be to secure timely, sustainable patient access to the company’s products by shaping the value narrative, and leading pricing and reimbursement strategies and execution across multiple international markets. This includes oversight of related dossiers, negotiations, and cost coverage approaches. In this role you ensure alignment of Market Access ambitions with clinical value and global pricing interdependencies.</p> <p>You will also be a core member of the International Market Access team, contributing to global decision-making and ensuring alignment across regions while representing diverse market perspectives.</p> <p>This role requires strong collaboration with cross-functional colleagues and external stakeholders across multiple countries to ensure high-quality execution and impact. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in Market Access processes across several international markets and experience introducing innovative therapies in a global biotech environment. You are eager to make a meaningful contribution in pre-launch and launch phases, particularly within rare diseases and orphan conditions, and bring strong communication skills, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>Responsibilities</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Represent the payer perspective within cross-functional, cross-regional commercialization teams thereby optimizing pricing and market access of the asset.</li> <li>Closely collaborate with HEOR and clusters' leadership teams, Marketing and Clinical Development counterparts to ensure value and access optimization for the asset.</li> <li>Lead early payer engagement with key HTA/payer bodies (e.g. NICE UK, G-BA Germany) to inform evidence generation strategy, value proposition and reimbursement dossiers development.</li> <li>Interact with internal and external experts in pricing, health economics, patient advocacy, health technology assessment authorities, government policy makers and payers as required to execute Pricing &amp; Reimbursement objectives.</li> <li>Provide hands-on support and train local access teams on negotiation strategy and ensure HTA and reimbursement submissions are aligned to the Global and International strategy.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>Where You’ll Work&nbsp; </u></strong></p> <p>This is an office role based and requires in-office collaboration 2-3x per week in our Zug Office.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>&nbsp;</u></strong><strong><u>Who You Are</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Extensive experience leading HTA submissions and pricing negotiations across multiple international markets, ideally including Europe and other global regions, particularly in rare diseases and orphan conditions.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of international healthcare systems, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and regulatory environments.</li> <li>Experience generating and leveraging data for HTA submissions and pricing negotiations, with a strong external network of agencies and stakeholders.</li> <li>Comfortable presenting at senior levels and engaging with external thought leaders globally.</li> <li>Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional and multicultural teams (including external partners).</li> <li>Knowledge of product commercialization processes with a hands-on, solution-oriented mindset for building scalable processes and documentation.</li> </ul> <p><strong><u>Rewarding Those Who Make the Mission Possible</u></strong></p> <p>We have high expectations for our team members. raw.description:
As Destinus scales its vehicle programmes, we are looking for a dedicated Technical Project Manager to own execution across the full vehicle development stack – from propulsion and structures through avionics integration, ground support equipment, and qualification. This frees our engineers to focus on technical depth and our team leads on strategic leadership.

As one of the first hires in this group, you will manage a programme and help build the PM structure itself alongside team leads and fellow TPMs. You own execution – schedule, cross-disciplinary coordination, risk, and delivery. The engineers run the technical depth; you run the programme.

What You’ll Do

· Own end-to-end execution of vehicle-level and subsystem product development programmes – from kick-off through hardware build, test campaigns, qualification, and delivery

· Build and maintain programme plans spanning propulsion, structures, avionics, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and regulatory dependencies; identify and resolve critical path risks early

· Run programme reviews and cross-functional coordination meetings; keep decisions documented and actions closed

· Work closely with engineering leads across disciplines to track technical progress and translate it into clear programme status

· Coordinate system integration activities – ensuring interfaces between subsystems (propulsion, structures, avionics, GSE) are managed, dependencies tracked, and integration milestones owned

· Manage external dependencies: supplier lead times, test facility scheduling, regulatory submissions, and customer milestones

· Proactively flag scope creep, resource conflicts, and schedule risk to leadership – with options, not just problems

· Contribute to building the PM structure, tools, and ways of working for the department alongside team leads and fellow TPMs

Requirements

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, systems, or a related engineering discipline

· 5–8 years in a hardware-heavy development environment; at least 2 in a project management, programme coordination, or technical lead role – career PMs without hardware exposure will not be considered

· Background in aerospace, defence, or a similarly regulated hardware domain; familiarity with vehicle-level or system-level development and qualification cycles is essential

· Experience managing cross-disciplinary programmes spanning multiple engineering domains (structures, propulsion, avionics, or similar) is a strong advantage

· Able to manage multiple concurrent projects across engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and testing

· Strong systems thinking – able to see the full picture, spot where the hard problems are likely to sit, and know when to dive into detail without losing the overall programme

· Strong planning skills – able to build a programme schedule from scratch, identify critical path, and keep it current

· Comfortable building structure in an ambiguous environment; pragmatic over bureaucratic

· Clear, direct communicator in English; German is an advantage

Über 7.000 Ärzte, medizinische Institute und Heilpraktiker arbeiten mit uns zusammen. Das macht FormMed zur Nr. 1 bei Ärzten und Therapeuten in Deutschland.

Es macht Spaß, bei uns zu arbeiten! Das Arbeitsumfeld ist trotz komplexer Anforderung menschlich und humorvoll, geprägt von Eigenverantwortung, kurzen Entscheidungswegen, schneller Umsetzung, langjährigen Mitarbeitern:innen und einer Führung durch Vertrauen. Wir verkaufen Gesundheit nicht nur nach außen, sondern leben sie auch nach innen. Du solltest diese Unternehmenskultur zu schätzen wissen und Dich bewusst dafür entscheiden.

Wegen unseres stetigen und schnellen Wachstums suchen wir viele neue Kollegen:innen, die uns noch weiter voranbringen und gut ins Team passen. Wachse mit uns und profitiere von einem Umfeld, das Dir große Sicherheit und viele Chancen bietet.


Deine Rolle

Du möchtest einen Markt nicht nur betreuen, sondern aktiv entwickeln und nachhaltige Partnerschaften aufbauen? Du verstehst Vertrieb als Beziehungsgeschäft mit Sinn – besonders im Gesundheitsumfeld?

FormMed steht für hochwertige Mikronährstofflösungen, wissenschaftliche Qualität und das gemeinsame Ziel, Gesundheit nachhaltig zu verbessern. In einem respektvollen, lernbereiten Umfeld arbeiten wir täglich daran, medizinische Expertise zugänglich zu machen und echte Wirkung zu erzielen.

Wenn du Vertrieb mit Purpose verbinden, Beziehungen aufbauen und einen Markt nachhaltig entwickeln möchtest, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.
Wir suchen ab sofort einen Senior Regional Account Manager Westschweiz (m/w/d) in unbefristeter Anstellung für eine Vollzeittätigkeit im Vertriebsteam mit Fokus auf den Schweizer Markt und insbesondere die Westschweiz.

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy, Intern
description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware. The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one. This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes. What You'll Work On Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities. Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather. Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer. Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts. Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions. Apply solid engineering practices: code review, version control, reproducible experiments and clear documentation. Who We're Looking For We're looking for a strong robotics student who wants to see their work run on real robots, not only in simulation. You don't need every item below, but you should meet the core requirements and bring depth in at least one area of the autonomy stack. You'll join a small team that moves fast, expects ownership, and holds work to the standard of running on live customer sites. Your Background Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD, or completed a Master's degree within the last year, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. Demonstrated depth in at least one of perception, localisation and state estimation, or motion planning and navigation, through a thesis, research or a substantial project. Strong coding skills in Python. Hands-on experience with ROS 2. Comfortable using Linux, Docker and Git in your workflows. Nice to Have Experience working with physical robots, ideally mobile or legged. Experience with lidar or camera processing, SLAM, or sensor fusion. Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo or MuJoCo. Publications or competition results in robotics (ICRA, IROS, RSS, CoRL). What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow. Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.
